title: Structural evaluation and exchange identities for the actual specialization factors
statement:
Use the finite coefficients $A=A_{E,n}$, lifts, and canonical nearby-cycle maps of [def-trf-deformation-specialization], with the normalized constructible operation datum of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. Let $c:C\to X\times_kX$ be a correspondence of separated finite-type $k$-schemes with a separated finite-type lift $\widetilde c$ over $D=\operatorname{Spec}(k[t]_{(t)})$. Choose the proper refinement $\widetilde c'\to\widetilde c$ and proper extension of $\widetilde c'$ supplied by [lem-trf-specialization-cohomological-comparison]. Write $b'=\widetilde c'_0$, $b=\widetilde c_0$. Let $(f_Z,t_Z,\alpha_g,\beta_g,\iota)$ be either the canonical specialization pre-comparison $c\to b'$ or the proper-direct-image comparison $b'\to b$. These are the actual factors of the canonical comparison, with the maps and finite-Tor domains supplied by that theorem; they are not arbitrary abstract pre-comparisons. Write $\bar c$ for the target of the chosen factor and use the notation $j_Z,r_Z,d_Z,\delta_Z,\Pi$ and the ordinary and exceptional mates of [def-trf-cohomological-comparison]. All the fixed-diagram exceptional operations are assumed admissible as in [def-trf-admissibility]. Then the following structural identities hold on the indicated finite-Tor constructible domains, without assuming that the specialization factor satisfies requirements (VI) and (VII) for every fibrewise proper arrow or has dense special-fibre compactification opens.

For an arrow $g:U\to V$ of the fixed diagram and $M,N\in D^b_{ctf}(V,A)$, use the exceptional tensor and internal-Hom maps $T_g,H_g$ defined by their counit and evaluation transposes in [lem-trf-cohomological-evaluation-calculus].

(a) Exceptional tensor compatibility:
$$\beta_g(M\otimes N)\circ f_U(T_g)\circ t_U\circ(1\otimes\alpha_g)=\bar g^!(t_V)\circ T_{\bar g}\circ(\beta_g\otimes1)$$
as maps $f_Ug^!M\otimes\bar g^*f_VN\to\bar g^!f_V(M\otimes N)$.

(b) Exceptional internal-Hom compatibility:
$$R\mathcal Hom(\alpha_g,\beta_g)\circ r_U\circ f_U(H_g)=H_{\bar g}\circ\bar g^!(r_V)\circ\beta_g$$
as maps $f_Ug^!R\mathcal Hom(M,N)\to R\mathcal Hom(\bar g^*f_VM,\bar g^!f_VN)$.

(c) Tensor unit and diagonal normalization:
$$t_Z\circ(1\otimes j_Z)=1_{f_ZM},\qquad\alpha_\Delta\circ\bar\Delta^*\Pi_{M,N}=t_X,$$
with $f_ZM\otimes A_{\bar Z}=f_ZM$ and $\Delta^*(M\boxtimes N)=M\otimes N$ [def-trf-external-product].



(d) Put $\chi:p_2^*\omega_X\to p_1^!A_X$ for the canonical exchange in the Cartesian square $X\times_kX$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ over $s$ (the leg order is the project's order). More explicitly, put $B_M=(\operatorname{Ex}_{!,a,a}(M))^{-1}:Rp_{1!}p_2^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}a_X^*Ra_{X!}M$, where the compact-support exchange is normalized as in [def-exchange-projection] and is invertible by [prop-functor-package](4). Define $\chi$ to be the $Rp_{1!}\dashv p_1^!$ transpose of $a_X^*(\varepsilon_{a_X,A_s}^!)\circ B_{\omega_X}$. Its barred counterpart is defined by the identical formula for the barred operations. Then
$$\beta_{p_1}(A_X)\circ f_{X\times X}(\chi)\circ\alpha_{p_2}(\omega_X)=p_{1,\bar X}^!(j_X)\circ\bar\chi\circ p_{2,\bar X}^*(\delta_X)$$
as maps $p_{2,\bar X}^*f_X\omega_X\to p_{1,\bar X}^!f_XA_X$.

(e) Exceptional composition: $\beta_{\operatorname{id}}=\operatorname{id}$ and $\beta_{hg}=\bar g^!(\beta_h)\circ\beta_g(h^!(-))$, under the exceptional composition identifications.

Dualizing composition: for every diagram arrow $g:U\to V$,
$$\delta_U=\bar g^!(\delta_V)\circ\beta_g(\omega_V)$$
under $g^!\omega_V=\omega_U$ and $\bar g^!\omega_{\bar V}=\omega_{\bar U}$ of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition].



(f) Let $h:U\to W$, $v:V\to W$, $U'=V\times_WU$, $h':U'\to V$, $v':U'\to U$ form a Cartesian square of arrows in the unbarred fixed diagram, and assume the corresponding barred square is Cartesian. Suppose $h,h',\bar h,\bar h'$ are proper. Let $E:Rh'_*v'^!\xrightarrow{\sim}v^!Rh_*$ and $\bar E:R\bar h'_*\bar v'^!\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar v^!R\bar h_*$ be the right-adjoint fixed-square exchange maps, normalized as mates of compact-support exchange. Then for every $M\in D^b_{ctf}(U,A)$,
$$\bar v^!(\alpha_{h,*})\circ\beta_v(Rh_*M)\circ f_V(E_M)=\bar E_{f_UM}\circ R\bar h'_*(\beta_{v'}(M))\circ\alpha_{h',*}(v'^!M)$$
as maps $f_VRh'_*v'^!M\to\bar v^!R\bar h_*f_UM$. For this last clause, on the specialization factor also require that the total lifts of $h,h'$ are proper. In particular the clause applies to $h=\Delta_X$, $v=c$, $h'=i_F$, $v'=d$ in the fixed square: the total diagonal and its base change are closed immersions. On the proper-direct-image factor the displayed properness of the four fibre maps suffices. These conclusions are structural identities; none asserts compatibility of a trace map or a trace class.
